issue.title: Audit low-alpha TUI colors for xterm-256 palette remapping
issue.description: The prompt-bar snippet-frame fix proved that low-alpha theme colors flattened over dark surfaces can downgrade into xterm-256 slots 16-21, which base16/base24 terminal palettes commonly remap to bright accents. After removing the two unsafe snippet fills, src/sase/ace/tui/styles.tcss still contains 15 percentage-alpha background declarations (including 6-12% warning fills and multiple 22-40% accent fills). Audit every remaining declaration in its actual compositing context, add a reusable palette-safety regression guard where appropriate, replace unsafe state encoding with opaque hue/weight treatments, and update only causally affected visual goldens. Keep terminal capability detection and forcing truecolor out of scope.

payload.entry: Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (requested by the project owner: keep the seven highest-impact open tasks, close the rest). These are per-node visual-snapshot stabilizations (artifacts/beads provider inventory, frontmatter panel, preview panel reference, the low-alpha xterm-256 palette audit) plus the just test-visual-update blast-radius defect. The PNG suite is excluded from 'just test' and 'just test-cov', so none of these blocks the shared check/check-full gates, and today's 'tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake' run names 12 reproducible flakes, none of them a PNG node. The update-mode hazard in sase-lo is real but mitigated by review discipline (goldens land in a diff). Re-file with a +1 if a golden mismatch blocks a landing.

payload.close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: PNG-golden drift is contained by the dedicated just test-visual lane and is not blocking the shared gates.
